root_cause.text: In `arch/powerpc/platforms/pseries/papr-hvpipe.c`, the stack-allocated `struct papr_hvpipe_hdr` was only partially initialized (`version` and `flags`), leaving its reserved/padding fields uninitialized and therefore leaking kernel stack bytes to userspace via `copy_to_user()`.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit message states that `hdr` is allocated on the stack, only `hdr.version` and `hdr.flags` were set, and `papr_hvpipe_hdr` contains `reserved[3]` and `reserved2[40]` fields that could expose uninitialized data; the patch fixes this by changing `struct papr_hvpipe_hdr hdr;` to `struct papr_hvpipe_hdr hdr = {};`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Zero-initialize the read-side header structure to prevent use of uninitialized stack contents.
intent_record.what: In `papr_hvpipe_handle_read()`, the local variable `struct papr_hvpipe_hdr hdr` was changed to be zero-initialized at declaration using `= {}` instead of being left uninitialized.
intent_record.how: This ensures all fields of the header structure start with deterministic zero values before use, preventing any reads of stale stack data and avoiding unintended behavior from partially filled headers.

grouping_result.intent: Zero-initialize the read-side header structure to prevent use of uninitialized stack contents.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause by zero-initializing the stack-allocated read-side header, which prevents leaking uninitialized reserved/padding bytes to userspace.

candidates.rationale: This stack-allocated header was used without being zero-initialized, so its reserved/padding bytes could remain uninitialized and later be copied to userspace, leaking kernel stack contents.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is not present here. The read path explicitly initializes the stack header before copying it out: `struct papr_hvpipe_hdr hdr;` followed by `hdr.version = 0;` and `hdr.flags = 0;`, then `copy_to_user(buf, &hdr, HVPIPE_HDR_LEN);`. This means the shown function does not leak uninitialized stack bytes through the header. The fix is already present because the code only exposes the initialized header fields and does not rely on partially initialized stack contents.
